title: A Simple and Rapid System for Proteomic Analysis of the Archaeon Candidatus Vulcanisaeta moutnovskia
protocol: Dissolve cell pellets in lysis buffer containing 8 M urea, 2 M thiourea, 5% CHAPS, 2 mM TCEP-HCl and protease inhibitor.
Homogenize the cells by ultrasonication (10 strokes, low amplitude) on ice.
Centrifuge the lysed cells at 20,000×g for 10 min at 4°C.
Use the supernatant containing solubilised proteins for LC-MS/MS experiment.
Determine total protein concentration using Pierce 660nm protein assay (Thermo).
Dilute an aliquot of every sample with loading sample buffer and apply onto a conventional SDS-PAGE gel with 1.2 cm wide wells.
Stop the run as soon as the front enters 1 cm into the resolving gel to concentrate the whole proteome at the stacking/resolving gel interface.
Wash gel plugs with 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate.
Wash gel plugs with ACN.
Reduce gel pieces with 10 mM DTT in 25 mM ammonium bicarbonate solution.
Alkylation was carried out with 55 mM IAA in 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate solution.
Rinse gel pieces with 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate.
Rinse gel pieces with ACN.
Dry gel pieces under a stream of nitrogen.
Add Proteomics Grade Trypsin at a final concentration of 16 ng/μl in 25% ACN/50 mM ammonium bicarbonate solution to the dried gel pieces.
Incubate the reaction mixture at 37°C for 4 h.
Stop the digestion by adding 50% ACN/0.5% TFA for peptide extraction.
Elute tryptic peptides and dry them using speed-vacuum centrifugation.
Desalt eluted peptides onto StageTip C18 Pipette tips until ready for mass spectrometric analysis.
Subject a 1 µg aliquot of each sample to 1D-nano LC ESI-MSMS analysis.
Use a nano liquid chromatography system coupled to a high-speed Triple TOF 5600 mass spectrometer with a Nanospray III source.
Load the analytical column, which is a silica-based reversed phase Acquity UPLC M-Class Peptide BEH C18 Column.
Trap the sample using a C18 Acclaim PepMapTM 100 trap column and switch it online with the analytical column.
Deliver a solution of 0.1% formic acid in water at 2 µl/min using the loading pump.
Provide a flow-rate of 250 nl/min using the nano-pump under gradient elution conditions.
Separate peptides using a 250-minute gradient ranging from 2% to 90% mobile phase B.
Inject a volume of 5 μl for analysis.
Dissolve cell pellets with multi-chaotropic lysis buffer containing 7 M urea, 2 M thiourea, 5% SDS, 100 mM TEAB, and a protease/phosphatase inhibitor cocktail.
Add 5 mM TCEP-HCl and 10 mM CAA to the dissolved cell pellets for reduction and alkylation at 37°C for 1 hour.
Homogenize samples by micro tip probe ultrasonication for 1 min using an UP50H ultrasonic lab homogenizer.
Centrifuge the homogenate at 16,000 × g for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Collect the supernatant containing solubilized proteins and estimate protein concentration by Pierce 660nm protein assay.
Dilute 20 µg of protein to 40 µL with 5% SDS.
Add 12% phosphoric acid to the diluted protein solution.
Add seven volumes of binding buffer (90% methanol; 100 mM TEAB) to achieve a final phosphoric acid concentration of 1.2%.
Load the protein solution onto an S-Trap filter in two consecutive steps, separated by a 2 min centrifugation at 3000 x g.
Wash the S-Trap filter three times with 150 µL of binding buffer.
Add 1 µg of Pierce MS-grade trypsin in 20 μL of a 100 mM TEAB solution to each sample (1:20 w/w ratio) and spin through the S-Trap.
Allow the samples to digest overnight at 37°C in a wet chamber.
Elute peptides using two step-wise buffers: first, apply 40 µL of 25 mM TEAB; then apply 40 µL of 80% acetonitrile and 0.2% formic acid in H₂O, separated by a 2 min centrifugation at 3000 x g.
Pool the eluted peptides and vacuum centrifuge to dryness.
Clean up/desalt digested samples using Stage-Tips with Empore 3M C18 disks.
Concentrate peptide solutions using Qubit™ Fluorometric Quantitation.
Subject 1 μg aliquot of each digested sample to 1D-nano LC-ESI-MS/MS analysis.
Elute peptides onto a 50 cm × 75 μm Easy-spray PepMap C18 analytical column at 45°C using a flow rate of 250 nL/min with a gradient from 2% to 95% mobile phase B over 210 min.
Acquire data using a top-15 method, in full scan positive mode, scanning 380 to 1800 m/z with a resolution of 60,000 at m/z 200 and an Automatic Gain Control (AGC) target of 3 × 10^6.
Select the top 15 most intense ions from each MS1 scan for fragmentation via higher energy collisional dissociation (CID).
Fragment selected ions with a resolution of 15,000 at m/z 200 and an AGC target of 2 × 10^5.
Isolate precursors with a window of 2 m/z and apply normalized collision energy (NCE) of 20.
Process MS/MS data using Analyst® TF 1.7 Software.
Convert raw data files into mgf files for further analysis.
Search mgf files against a protein database including "Candidatus V. moutnovskia" and Thermoproteus uzoniensis sequences from Uniprot/Swissprot Knowledgebase.
Set search parameters to include trypsin as enzyme with up to 2 missed cleavages allowed.
Apply carbamidomethyl (C) as fixed modification and acetyl (Protein N-term), Gln to pyro-Glu (N-term Q), Glu to pyro-Glu (N-term E), and Oxidation (M) as variable modifications.
Set peptide mass tolerance to 25 ppm for Method I and ±10 ppm for Method II.
Set fragment masses tolerance to 0.05 Da for Method I and 0.02 Da for Method II.
Ensure protein identification confidence interval is ≥95% (p<0.05).
Consider only peptides with an individual ion score above the 1% False Discovery Rates (FDR) at spectra level as correctly identified.
